newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Uzbekistan Air to double ex-Amsterdam cargo capacity.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan Air to double ex-Amsterdam cargo capacity.

text.p: Uzbekistan Airways is to more than double cargo capacity ex-Netherlands from June 3 when a Boeing 767-300ER will replace a twice-weekly Airbus Industrie A310 service to New York, a spokesman for the carrier's Dutch gsa, Air Support, said.
The service will operate Tashkent-Amsterdam-New York and the 767 will offer in excess of 15 tonnes capacity per flight compared to seven tonnes previously, the spokesman, Carlo de Haas, told Reuters.

Air Support is also the Dutch gsa for Aeroflot. He said major shipments to Uzbekistan include computers, spare parts and machinery while flowers are also a major import and added that other CIS countries are importing flowers from the Netherlands.

Countries such as Georgia, Russia as well as Estonia, are buying flowers directly from countries such as Ecuador. The flowers are flown from Latin America to the Netherlands where they are pre-cooled and labelled before onward shipment, Haas said.
"In these countries people are very fond of the large, long- stemmed red roses and they buy them directly from Latin American countries," said de Haas.
However, as they are buying direct from the countries, this also means that they do not go via the Aalsmeer Flower Auction, he added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
